# Question nr. 3

# Comparing PD-1, T-cell-inflamed GEP and TMB – how they relate to immunotherapy response

tasks:

1.  Visualize the distribution of each biomarker in responders vs non-responders (boxplots).
2.  Test whether each biomarker differs significantly between response groups.
3.  Compare the direction and magnitude of the differences, and discuss which biomarkers show stronger associations.
4.  Explain the biological information captured by each biomarker and discuss strengths and limitations.

## Load the libraries + data

```{r}
library(ggplot2)
library(patchwork)

# folder with the data (change here if the path is different)
data_dir <- "../22123_cpm/CPM_G4/data"

#counts   <- readRDS(file.path(data_dir, "counts.rds"))
#tpm      <- readRDS(file.path(data_dir, "tpm.rds"))
#clinical <- readRDS(file.path(data_dir, "clinical.rds"))

counts <- readRDS("../data/counts.rds")
tpm <- readRDS("../data/tpm.rds")
clinical <- readRDS("../data/clinical.rds")
# checking the columns
colnames(clinical)
head(clinical)
```

```{r}
# column with sample id
sample_col <- "sample_id"

# column with Best Overall Response
resp_col <- "BOR"

# defining responder vs non-responder
responder_values     <- c("R")
non_responder_values <- c("NR")

# TMB column in clinical
tmb_col <- "TMB"
#tpm 
# TPM is normalized (gene length + depth) but on a LINEAR scale, so we log2 it
log_transform_tpm <- TRUE

group_colours <- c("Non-responder" = "#D9534F", "Responder" = "#2E86C1")
```

## Matching the samples

```{r}
resp_raw <- as.character(clinical[[resp_col]])
resp <- ifelse(resp_raw %in% responder_values, "Responder",
               ifelse(resp_raw %in% non_responder_values, "Non-responder", NA))

clinical$Response <- factor(resp, levels = c("Non-responder", "Responder"))

cat("Distribution of responses:\n")
print(table(clinical$Response, useNA = "ifany"))

# leave only the samples with one, concrete response
keep_resp <- !is.na(clinical$Response)
clinical  <- clinical[keep_resp, ]
ids       <- as.character(clinical[[sample_col]])

# TPM columns in the same order as clinical
stopifnot(all(ids %in% colnames(tpm)))
tpm <- tpm[, ids, drop = FALSE]
stopifnot(identical(colnames(tpm), ids))
```

## Separating 3 biomarkers

```{r}
# PD-1 = PDCD1 — raw TPM (NO log2), to match RQ4
pd1 <- as.numeric(tpm["PDCD1", ])

# T-cell-inflamed GEP — 19-gene list (incl. PDCD1), log2(TPM+1), to match RQ4
gep_genes <- c("TIGIT","CD27","CD8A","PDCD1LG2","LAG3","CD274","CXCR6","CMKLR1",
               "NKG7","CCL5","PSMB10","IDO1","CXCL9","HLA-DQA1","CD276","STAT1",
               "HLA-DRB1","HLA-E","PDCD1")
gep_present <- gep_genes[gep_genes %in% rownames(tpm)]
cat("Found GEP genes:", length(gep_present), "of", length(gep_genes), "\n")

# log2 only for GEP, then z-score per gene, then mean across genes
gep_expr   <- log2(tpm[gep_present, , drop = FALSE] + 1)
gep_scaled <- t(scale(t(gep_expr)))
gep_score  <- colMeans(gep_scaled, na.rm = TRUE)

# TMB from clinical data
if (!is.na(tmb_col)) {
  tmb <- as.numeric(clinical[[tmb_col]])
} else {
  tmb <- rep(NA_real_, nrow(clinical))
}

# one data frame for analysis
df <- data.frame(
  sample   = ids,
  Response = clinical$Response,
  PDCD1    = pd1,
  GEP      = gep_score,
  TMB      = tmb
)
head(df)
```

## Box plots

Each biomarker in response groups + Wilcoxon test

```{r}
# boxplot + jitter + p-value from Wilcoxon test

plot_biomarker <- function(data, var, ylab) {
  d  <- data[!is.na(data[[var]]), ]
  wt <- wilcox.test(d[[var]] ~ d$Response, exact = FALSE)
  ggplot(d, aes(x = Response, y = .data[[var]], fill = Response)) +
    geom_boxplot(width = 0.6, outlier.shape = NA, alpha = 0.7) +
    geom_jitter(width = 0.12, alpha = 0.6, size = 1.2) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = group_colours) +
    # short x-axis labels so they don't overlap
    scale_x_discrete(labels = c("Non-responder" = "NR", "Responder" = "R")) +
    guides(fill = "none") +
    labs(x = NULL, y = ylab,
         subtitle = paste0("Wilcoxon p = ", signif(wt$p.value, 3))) +
    theme_classic(base_size = 11) +
    theme(plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 9))
}

p_pd1 <- plot_biomarker(df, "PDCD1", "PDCD1 (PD-1), TPM")
p_gep <- plot_biomarker(df, "GEP",   "T-cell–inflamed GEP score")
p_tmb <- plot_biomarker(df, "TMB",   "TMB (mut/Mb)")

combined_plot <- p_pd1 + p_gep + p_tmb   # 3 panels next to each other
combined_plot
```

## Table with results

For each biomarker we report the group mediansnd and the Wilcoxon p-value

```{r}
summarise_biomarker <- function(data, var) {
  d   <- data[!is.na(data[[var]]), ]
  med <- tapply(d[[var]], d$Response, median)
  wt  <- wilcox.test(d[[var]] ~ d$Response, exact = FALSE)
  data.frame(
    Biomarker      = var,
    n_NonResponder = sum(d$Response == "Non-responder"),
    n_Responder    = sum(d$Response == "Responder"),
    median_NonResp = round(med["Non-responder"], 3),
    median_Resp    = round(med["Responder"], 3),
    direction      = ifelse(med["Responder"] > med["Non-responder"],
                            "higher in responders", "higher in non-responders"),
    wilcox_p       = signif(wt$p.value, 3)
  )
}

results <- do.call(rbind, lapply(c("PDCD1", "GEP", "TMB"),
                                 function(v) summarise_biomarker(df, v)))
rownames(results) <- NULL
results
```

## conclusion

all three candidate biomarkers (PD-1, the 18 genes T cell inflamed GEP and TMB) were higher in responders than non responders and each of them differed significantly between two response groups. Proof for that showed wilcoxon test with p\<0.001 for all of three, as it is seen in boxplot or summarytable

when it comes to the direction, TMB showed the largest relative shift (median 7 -\> 14 mut/mb) and the strongest statistical evidence. GEP has the cleanest sepration of the two groups, which is seen on the boxplot-\> the boxes barely overlapping. PD-1 showed the weakest assosiation out of all of them, with the most overlap between the groups.

the “strongest” biomarker depends on the criterion used: TMB wins on p-value and relative median change, whereas GEP best separates the groups visually. All of the 3 biomarkers represend very low p value.

when it comes to investigate biological meaning- each biomarker reflects a different part of the anti tumor immune response. TMB is a genomic measure of the number of somatic mutations. Pd-1 is a single gene read out activated/exhausted T cells. The T cell inflamed GEP summarizes a coordinated, multi-gene signal of an inflamed tumor microenvironment.

Limitations: these are group level associations in baseline samples, not balidated predictive biomarkers, so some of them overlap. Groups are strongly imbalanced between responders and nonresponders

To sum up, all three biomarkers are associated with response, with the strongest and largest relative effect for TMB and the cleanest group separation for GEP, but the overlapping distributions, imbalanced mean these should be interpreted as associations rather than clinically actionable predictors..
